page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.large is a general-purpose virtual server built on the x86_64 architecture using a dedicated AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The configuration provides 1 physical core delivering 2 vCPUs via hyper-threading, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Advanced instruction set support encompasses AVX-512 extensions (including AVX512_VNNI and AVX512_BF16) alongside AES and SHA_NI cryptographic capabilities. The instance includes no local block storage and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluation demonstrates high single-threaded compute output alongside expected multi-core scaling limitations. In stress-ng single-core tests, the server achieves a top-tier score of 3111.39, complemented by a strong Geekbench single-core score of 2006.0. However, due to its low vCPU count, multi-core metrics fall into lower performance brackets, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 3112.08 and a PassMark CPU score of 3861.67. Memory performance testing records average bandwidth speeds of 47.71 GB/sec for uncached large reads and 27.73 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific tests reveal lower relative throughput in static web serving (2.73 GB/sec) and database operations.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM configuration delivers balanced memory capacity for small-scale applications, offering strong individual core throughput without paying for unused multi-core capacity. The lack of local NVMe storage requires attachment of network storage for persistent data. This hardware profile provides qualitative efficiency for light compute tasks, single-threaded processing jobs, basic API endpoints, microservices, and general-purpose development or testing environments.

With a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.g8ae.large provides qualitative resource efficiency for lightweight general-purpose applications, microservices, micro-tier web servers, and single-threaded utility processing.
